newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - St. Jude stands by estimates.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - St. Jude stands by estimates.

text.p: St. Jude Medical Inc said Wednesday it remains comfortable with earnings per share forecasts in the low $0.30s for the second quarter and $1.40-$1.50 for the full year.

In an interview with Reuters following remarks to investors at a Piper Jaffray conference here, acting Chief Financial Officer Terry Shepherd said, "What we said ... was low 30s (for the second quarter), and that's been three weeks ago, and nothing's really changed since then. We couldn't provide any more detailed guidance than that."
The St. Paul, Minn.-based medical devices maker earned $0.32 per share in the second quarter of 1996.

Once largely a maker of heart valves, St. Jude in the past two and a half years has bought its way into the growing and highly competitive markets for pacemakers and implantable defibrillators, or ICDs. Both are electronic devices that regulate heartbeat.

Agreements last October to acquire Ventritex Inc and Telectronics Pacing Systems have transformed St. Jude, making year-ago earnings comparisons problematic and presenting management with a turning point.
On the 1997 earnings outlook, Shepherd said, "We said $1.40 to $1.50 (three weeks ago at an analysts' meeting). Nothing has structurally changed."

However, he said, much hangs in the balance as St. Jude folds Ventritex and Telectronics into its business. "The only thing that could move that (earnings estimate range) up or down is how rapidly ... we deploy the ICD technology to the bigger sales force," he said.
A jump in St. Jude sales and earnings is expected by analysts when it unleashes its 400-person sales force with the full Ventritex ICD product line.

Ventritex's devices remain competitive but suffered for years from inadequate sales support. That weakness will likely vanish with St. Jude's help -- a prospect likely causing some concern at ICD market rivals Medtronic Inc and Guidant Corp -- but timing remains uncertain.

"We're not going to be irresponsible about deploying that technology," Shepherd said. "We're not going to do it three months ahead of time just to get a number in the second quarter -- or third quarter or fourth quarter -- if in fact we're not satisfied that the reps are capable of dealing with implants. We're going to do the right thing."

According to Salomon Brothers medical technology analyst Eli Kammerman, the Ventritex deal will reduce St. Jude's 1997 earnings by about $0.30 per share, to $1.42, due to dilution, but ICD sales will boost 1998 earnings to $2.10 per share.
